data.name: Amber's Magic Shop
data.detailed_description:
Um conto de fadas mais sombrio: desta vez, o cenário é muito mais sombrio do que nos jogos anteriores.

CARACTERÍSTICAS DO JOGO

  • Com mais de 35 CGs e imagens sexy, um dos maiores jogos da Winter Wolves até agora!
  • Jogue como a elfa negra Amber em uma simulação de relacionamento/ofício em um mundo sombrio/gótico
  • Três romances otome (Daniel, Bernard & Lair), um romance yuri (Ruby)
  • E pela primeira vez, dois romances poli (Cosmina e Lynn)
  • Minijogo de construção de loja: construa sua própria "loja mágica"!


Estude e descubra novas receitas

Recolha ingredientes

Produza para ganhar dinheiro e experiência

Amber, uma elfa negra, foi abandonada ainda bebê nas florestas ao sul de Icesilia. Ela foi encontrada e criada por Vin, uma bruxa, que decidiu que ela deveria se tornar uma alquimista. Quando Amber completou dezesseis anos, Vin a enviou para Icesilia como aprendiz do lendário mago Haros.

Na grande cidade de Icesilia, ela vai treinar e, quando atingir a maioridade, se tornará uma mestre alquimista que dirige sua própria loja, e ao longo do caminho, também conhecerá personagens interessantes que podem se tornar algo mais do que apenas amigos:

  • Daniel, filho de Haros, que quer ser um mago como seu pai, mas também treina em alquimia. Em competição com Amber desde a juventude, ele precisará ter cuidado para não ser consumido pelo orgulho.
  • Bernard, um jovem bravo que quer se tornar um aventureiro famoso. Paranoico e mal-humorado, ele precisará aprender a se controlar para evitar fazer coisas das quais possa se arrepender.
  • Lair, filho do influente nobre elfo Arnor. Ingênuo, mas de bom coração, sofre a má influência de seu arrogante pai Arnor.
  • Ruby, uma jovem sedutora que se tornou vampira recentemente, lutando para não perder a humanidade que ainda resta nela.
  • Cosa e Anders, dois misteriosos aventureiros de cabelos prateados que pedirão ajuda a Amber e podem se revelar algo mais do que parecem.
  • Lynn, uma fofa elfa que administra a loja de ervas com sua mãe. Um casamento com um nobre foi arranjado para ela, mas ela não tem certeza se realmente o deseja.

O jogo pode ser jogado como um simulador de namoro e oferece um jogo de criação/simulação opcional. Cada escolha mudará a alinhamento de Amber (e de seus amigos/interesses amorosos): há o lado sombrio e o lado claro. Mas tenha cuidado: o lado sombrio e o lado claro não significam certo ou errado. Não há escolhas certas ou erradas neste jogo, embora alguns finais sejam mais tristes e cruéis do que outros!

O jogo apresenta 4 finais diferentes para cada interesse amoroso, com alguns eventos/cenas sombrios nunca antes vistos em um jogo da Winterwolves. Jogue o jogo por sua própria conta e risco! Desbloqueie todos os finais de um personagem específico para descobrir imagens bônus.

reviews.review:
"Amber's Magic Shop" is another visual novel from Winter Wolves, that I just can't recommend. 

[h1]Art.  [/h1]
I like the art style, although it is a bit inconsistent (different art styles for different characters). I like how characters grow, not only in description, but their sprites also reflects that [spoiler] Why Lair's though? Wasn't he like 70 already?[/spoiler] What I don't get are those panty shots and pin-ups. I'm more than fine with some teasing and even straight up adult content, but usually images like that fit to the context of the game. "Amber's Magic Shop" isn't too much focused on sex (although it seems to try). It's just a very plain romance story with fantasy setting, tiring alchemy sections and "main plot" going on in the background. 

[h1]Characters. [/h1]
Good ideas, that came out wrong. You have prince with daddy issues, you have your best friend, who should marry said prince, you have vampire that wants to be human, mercenary, that has too high ambitions and gets more and more paranoid, you have two relatives in love and your mentor's son. All of that could be a start of a great story and interesting relationships. Sadly, characters are very one-dimensional and inconsistent. For example, Lair [spoiler] who, despite his age, blushes and stutters just because Amber decided to wear more revealing dress, has no issues whatsoever, to undress his fiance in the public library AND without her explicit consent[/spoiler]. Also, we don't have enough time to get to know these characters. You met each of them about ten times during the game and every one of those meetings is short and very rarely offers anything interesting.

[h1]Story. [/h1]
It's nothing outstanding, but the core concept is fine. You're an alchemist. There's a blight. Find a cure for the blight. All of that would be good, if not for the cardinal sin of this game, which is...

[h1]Terrible writing. [/h1]
It's shocking. I mean, this is a 20€ visual novel form experienced studio, yet there were times, when I was just shaking my head, baffled by what I was reading. Dialogues are awful. Characters repeat each other way to often. For example (it's not quote from the game, but my take on character repeating themselves, which happens all the time):
A: I like it.
B: Okay. I was curious.
A: I know. I just like it.
There are ton of situations like that. Not only that, most of conversations are just boring and lead to nothing, other than giving us, ultimately meaningless, choice. 

[h1]Sex scenes. [/h1]
Part of the poor writing. They are literally the worst. I either felt highly uncomfortable [spoiler] Lynn and Lair's library scene[/spoiler] or confused [spoiler]Amber's night with Camosa and Reed[/spoiler]. Some of them came out of nowhere, other felt like they were written as a part of some terrible fanfiction. I expected Amber to have form some sort of bond with these characters. And I expected a choice. This game gives you neither.

[h1]Break-up scenes. [/h1]
I like the idea. I really do. Some of it was nicely done, especially when you chose to break up with someone later on (after, you know, you actually DID date them). But early on? I was so confused when Amber said to Daniel (who I had like one or two scenes in her adult life so far and it was mentioned that they haven't see each other very often), that they need to stop dating. And he seemed genuinely disappointed. I'm sorry, when exactly this whole "dating" thing happen? Why have I not seen it? Same goes for Bernard. God, guy just asked me to make him some stupid talisman, was pushy and unfriendly and somehow I find out that we were actually going out? It's extremely confusing.

[h1]Endings.[/h1]
Not only are they sudden, unsatisfying and without any real build-up. Not only "main story" endings are just few sentences of description, that do not link in any way with your romance ending. Not only you don't get any epilogue or nothing of that sort. No. Even romance endings are terrible. Bernard light plus endings, is not only extremely cliche, but done so badly, that I was surprised that's even possible [spoiler] Oh, so you tell me you suddenly found out that you're in love with me. And we just going to get it on, without discussing your behavior and growing paranoia. Great! It's nice to know, that all those conversations were really building up to something![/spoiler]. There are "dark" and "light" endings and, again, I like the core concept, but someone clearly didn't think this through. You can't have dramatic moments without relationship that you're invested in or characters that you care about.

[h1]Protagonist.[/h1] 
All I know about Amber is that she is dark elf, raised by a witch, that likes alchemy and is, apparently, dating half of the town. I have no idea what sort of personality she has and choices the game gave me didn't allow me to shape her in any meaningful way. 

[h1]Alchemy system. [/h1]
This is something that many people will have issues with, but for me, it was really the minor offence, compared with other faults that this game posses. You can turn it off, but I don't recommend it, since the whole balance of the story is off and the game finishes almost as quickly as it begun - especially if you disable some romance options. Again, that was a nice idea. I like mini games in visual novels, I like stat raising, I like all of that, when it's well done. Here, I was bored to death and annoyed. Instead of giving us option to try different ingredients and see what comes of it, instead of giving us some form of market and more clients and option to actually, you know, RUN our "Magic Shop" (it's in the tittle, God damn it!), you start by preparing for test and then have one client few other days with repeating, boring recipes that you've done dozens of times already.

[b]In short: Really bad writing, tiring alchemy system, bland characters and lack of actual romance. Not worth buying, unless on big discount.[/b]
